title: heuristic-probation-flags-for-runtime-candidate-danielle-cho
content:
Quick personal canvas for thinking about early probation signals if we hire this candidate (A.K.A. what to watch for in first 90 days). Not a final onboarding plan — more like heuristics to decide success vs remediation.

Context
- Candidate: senior runtime engineer (final loop on 2025-11-01). Strong ML infra background, previously led inference optimization at a midsize company. Technical interviewers: Samir (serving runtime), Maya (SRE/design), Ravi (performance kernel Q&A).
- Interview summary in 1 line: thoughtful tradeoff reasoning, decent systems instincts, hand-wavy on operational processes (incidents, playbooks), limited exposure to our batching/cache patterns.

Why write this: hiring committee undecided between green (hire) and amber (hire-with-targets). I want concrete signals we can measure early if we bring them on — to avoid surprises and to define coaching targets.

Concrete probation signals (metrics + qualitative)
1) First on-call rotation readiness (30 days)
   - Signal: can independently own at least one low-criticality on-call rotation and execute a postmortem without heavy hand-holding.
   - Measurement: ownership of 2 incidents (pager/alert triage) in first 30 days, drafts postmortems with proposed root cause and remediation plan within 72h.
   - Red flag: requires >2 scheduled pairing sessions to understand alerting and runbooks, or repeatedly misses follow-up items from incident RCA.

2) Baseline change landed to a running service (45 days)
   - Signal: authors and ships a small-but-impactful change to the serving runtime (e.g., config flag, a metric, small batching tweak) end-to-end (PR -> rollout -> monitor).
   - Measurement: PR with tests, rollout notes in release doc, dashboard showing expected metric delta (latency, error rate, throughput) and no regressions.
   - Red flag: PR blocked >2 weeks on basic review comments or requires constant reviewer hand-holding on CI/build issues.

3) Observable thinking in performance tradeoffs (60 days)
   - Signal: can explain a quantization/throughput tradeoff and propose a test plan to validate it on our infra.
   - Measurement: a short design note in Confluence or ticket outlining experiment, expected metrics, and rollback criteria.
   - Red flag: proposes vague experiments without thresholds or needs mentor to draft all acceptance criteria.

4) Collaboration & communication (qualitative, ongoing)
   - Signal: participates in design reviews, gives constructive feedback, and responds within our team SLAs on async threads.
   - Measurement: 3 PR reviews with substantive comments; responds to async threads within 48 hours; asks clarifying questions rather than only stating opinions.
   - Red flag: defensive in reviews, repeated missed syncs, or no follow-through on agreed action items.

5) Familiarity with our rollout and fallback policies (90 days)
   - Signal: demonstrates understanding of canary/rollback flow and can implement a simple canary policy change (e.g., adjust traffic split or fallback variant routing).
   - Measurement: ticket implementing a policy tweak, includes tests or simulated rollouts in staging, and integrates with Redwood Console hooks.
   - Red flag: misunderstands rollback surface area (e.g., conflates model variant compatibility with routing constraints) or requires step-by-step instructions for routine rollback.

Onboarding & coaching plan (short bullets)
- Week 0-2: pair onpager runbook walkthrough + sandbox incident simulation (runbook drills). Samir to pair first week.
- Week 3-6: small change (config/telemetry) assigned with buddy reviewer; require a pre-merge checklist item for rollout plan.
- Month 2: assign ownership of a performance experiment; expect a one-page experiment summary.
- Month 3: evaluate against signals above; decide whether to convert to full ownership path or extend coaching.

Interview-specific notes (raw)
- Kernel/latency Qs: good intuition on memory vs compute tradeoffs; used a simple example for KV cache sizing that showed systems thinking. Couldn't recall details of our continuous batching approach — said they'd 'read the runtime docs' and prototype.
- Incident response: described a past PCI incident where they coordinated mitigations but deferred root cause to another team. Leaned operations-wise (coordination) but less on instrumentation-driven RCA.
- Design prompt (scaling short-lived requests): proposed autoscaling + queue shaping; missed suggestion to leverage prefix caching for repeated user queries.
- Cultural fit: calm, asks good clarifying Qs, communicates tradeoffs. Not super proactive about process details in interview (could be interviewer bias).

Suggested scoring rubric for committee (my rough pick)
- Technical depth (0-5): 4
- System design & ownership (0-5): 3
- Ops / Oncall readiness (0-5): 2.5
- Communication & collaboration (0-5): 4
- Overall readiness for independent ownership (0-5): 3
- My recommendation: hire with a 90-day probation plan with the above signals; prefer candidate to start on a team with strong mentorship (Samir/Maya).

Open questions for hiring committee / followups
- Should we require an explicit SLA-readiness session before granting full oncall privileges? (I lean yes for this hire)
- Are there specific internal docs (playbooks) we want them to complete acknowledgement for? I propose: oncall runbook, canary rollback checklist, privacy/SOPs read.
- Do we want a written probation checklist to be attached to their offer (for transparency)? Pros: clarity; Cons: overly formal. I lean to attach a lightweight checklist.

Action items
- If we hire: create a 90-day probation ticket and assign Samir as mentor (owner) — link to JIRA-RUNTIME-1293.
- If committee wants remediation instead of hire: recommend a "contract-to-hire" 8-week trial with explicit deliverables.

Random notes to self (brain dump)
- Watch for attitude when asked to follow existing process vs re-inventing it — both can be good but we need someone who can ship first and refactor later.
- Good to pair early with infra team to accelerate understanding of our batching implementation.

---
End of scratchpad. Keep this lightweight and editable. I'll convert into a formal 90-day checklist if committee leans hire.
